note: R1 (docs/audits/2026-08-11-bug-triage.md), regression — a saga leg's own `with:` mapping can resolve a value (Transfer.Request's own `reference:`, forwarded onto Account::Debit/Account::Credit purely for saga correlation) that the TARGET command never declares as an attribute at all. Before the fix, `orchestrate.rs`'s `split_routed_args` only ever removed the ONE key it promoted into `to:`, leaving every OTHER undeclared key (here, `reference`) sitting in the projected args unfiltered — `Json::overlay` then carried it straight through into the persisted event, since its own `patch` (the typed args struct's `to_json()`) never touches a key it doesn't declare. Ruby's own `ReactionInvocation.command_facts` (`args.slice(*declared)`) never lets it through in the first place, so Ruby's own `AccountDebited`/`AccountCredited` events never carry a `reference` key. Confirmed live against the full corpus (spec/corpus/banking.json) before this fix: exactly 6 events differed this same way. This fixture pins the smallest reproduction — one transfer, one debit leg, one credit leg — as a permanent regression guard on the 3 pinned CI fixtures, not just the full corpus.
